title: Filtering Records
prompt: Find products above a specified price and students who achieved a given minimum score. Use the included PostgreSQL lab schema and synthetic data. Explain one edge case and do not run data-changing statements against production.
objective: Demonstrate filtering records with a correct, explainable SQL result.

starter.code:
-- Write a PostgreSQL query for this task.
-- Keep the output deterministic and explain the expected rows.

expected_output: Two filtered result sets show products above a price threshold and students at or above a mark threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Use SQL constructs appropriate for filtering records.
Use explicit joins, grouping, ordering, or predicates where they affect correctness.
Explain expected output and one edge case; keep all data changes inside a disposable lab or rollback transaction.
hints: Write the expected output shape first: one row per what?
Use a small subset of the included seed data to inspect the behavior.
Run the result against PostgreSQL in a disposable lab; the current CodeLeaf scaffold does not execute arbitrary SQL.
grading_method: Server-side SQL-token smoke check; it does not parse SQL or prove behavior. Human review and real PostgreSQL tests are required before publishing.
retry_policy: Allow retries. XP remains platform-controlled and only a correct server-side check can complete the exercise.
status_note: Practical exercise derived from Section C of the source PDF. Token grading is only a smoke check; validate the solution manually before publication.
